Performs the core logical compatibility proof for methods: it builds trait-to-impl substitutions and a hybrid parameter environment from impl- and trait-level predicates, normalizes them, and registers obligations showing the impl method’s bounds and signature are implied by the trait contract; on signature mismatch it calls `report_trait_method_mismatch`.
Returns the `TyCtxt` carried by `RemapLateBound` for use by the `TypeFolder` implementation; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Rewrites late-bound regions using the folder’s mapping, producing a new late-bound region when a remap exists and otherwise leaving the region unchanged; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Checks that an impl for an async trait method is itself async-compatible by allowing either `async fn` lowering to an opaque future or an existing error, and otherwise emitting a diagnostic; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Collects and normalizes RPITIT-related return-position types for an impl method by reconstructing the trait/impl mapping and obligation context; before doing substitution-sensitive work, it calls `check_method_is_structurally_compatible` as a safety gate.
Constructs an `ImplTraitInTraitCollector` with an empty type map and the supplied obligation context, span, parameter environment, and body id; it does not call other methods from the listed file.
Returns the `TyCtxt` from the collector’s inference context for use by its `TypeFolder` implementation; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Replaces trait `impl Trait` projections with fresh inference variables, caches them, recursively folds and normalizes their explicit bounds, and registers the resulting obligations; it calls its own `interner` helper while processing nested bounds.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in `RemapHiddenTyRegions` for use by the fallible folder; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Recursively remaps regions inside opaque types while preserving uncaptured bivariant lifetime arguments, rebuilding the opaque with transformed arguments when needed; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Remaps eligible late- and non-impl early-bound regions to identity early-bound regions using a stored map, and emits an error when the hidden type captures a lifetime not allowed by the trait definition; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Builds the detailed E0053 diagnostic for an impl method whose type does not match the trait method, deriving spans and tailored suggestions for receiver, argument, and return mismatches; it calls `extract_spans_for_error_reporting` to choose the relevant impl and trait spans.

Validates that the impl item and trait item have compatible lifetime-parameter structure and outlives-bound shape, emitting a targeted diagnostic when early-bound lifetime counts diverge; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Selects the most relevant impl and trait spans for a method type mismatch, using the mismatching argument or return position when possible and otherwise falling back to the obligation cause and trait item span; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Checks whether trait and impl methods agree on having a self parameter and on the receiver form, synthesizing readable `self` descriptions for diagnostics when they differ; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Compares the number of type and const generic parameters declared by the trait and impl associated items, with special handling to avoid duplicate RPITIT diagnostics, and emits an error when counts differ; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Checks that the impl method and trait method have the same number of parameters and reports a focused diagnostic spanning the argument list or fallback item span when they do not; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Verifies that corresponding type parameters in trait and impl methods agree on whether they are synthetic `impl Trait` generics, and emits E0643 with suggestions for converting between explicit generics and `impl Trait` when they differ; it contains a local visitor implementation but does not call other top-level methods from the listed file.
Walks a HIR type subtree and records the span of a matching type-parameter use when it finds the target resolved type parameter; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Ensures corresponding non-lifetime generic parameters in the impl and trait item have compatible kinds and const parameter types, emitting E0053 when a type parameter is matched with a const parameter or const types differ; it calls `assoc_item_kind_str` to format the diagnostic.

Top-level entry point for associated const compatibility checking: it resolves the impl’s trait reference and then calls `compare_number_of_generics`, `compare_generic_param_kinds`, and `compare_const_predicate_entailment`.

Top-level entry point for associated type compatibility checking: it calls `compare_number_of_generics`, `compare_generic_param_kinds`, `compare_type_predicate_entailment`, and `check_type_bounds` to validate generics, entailment, and declared bounds.

Proves that the impl associated type’s own predicates follow from the impl header plus the trait associated type predicates by building a hybrid parameter environment, normalizing, and solving obligations; it calls `check_region_bounds_on_impl_item` first.

Checks that the concrete impl associated type satisfies all explicit bounds declared on the trait associated type, constructing obligations under the impl parameter environment and extra GAT/RPITIT projection assumptions; it calls `param_env_with_gat_bounds` to augment the environment used for bound checking.
Returns a human-readable kind string (`const`, `method`, or `type`) for an associated item, primarily for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the listed file.

Collects region-resolution failures that point at impl method argument or return types, maps late-bound region names from the trait signature onto the impl signature, and then identifies impl inputs/outputs whose types appear in the recorded blame set so diagnostics can suggest replacing them with the trait’s corresponding type. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Emits the IMPLIED_BOUNDS_ENTAILMENT lint for an impl method, choosing either the method span or the spans of offending arguments, and adds a multipart suggestion when replacement text is available for bad argument or return types. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/context.rs:: Destructures a `TypeAndMut<'tcx>` into its `ty` and `mutbl` components for the `TyCtxt` interner interface. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Initializes a fresh `CtxtInterners` with the provided arena and default-created interning tables by repeatedly calling `Default::default`.

Interns a `TyKind` into the type interner, computing flags with `FlagComputation::for_kind`, computing a cached stable hash via `CtxtInterners::stable_hash`, allocating cached metadata in the arena with `alloc`, and wrapping the result with `Interned::new_unchecked`.

Computes a stable fingerprint unless inference vars are present or incremental compilation is disabled; it checks `intersects` and `is_none`, otherwise creates hashing contexts with `StableHasher::new` and `StableHashingContext::new`, hashes via `hash_stable`, and finalizes with `finish`.

Interns a predicate binder into the predicate interner, computing flags with `FlagComputation::for_predicate`, computing a cached stable hash via `CtxtInterners::stable_hash`, allocating cached metadata in the arena with `alloc`, and wrapping the result with `Interned::new_unchecked`.

Builds the pre-interned common type set by repeatedly calling `CtxtInterners::intern_ty` through a local `mk` closure, using iterator `map`/`collect` to precreate inference and fresh types, and using `List::empty` for the unit tuple.

Builds the pre-interned common region set by interning regions through the region interner with `intern`, allocating them with `alloc`, wrapping them with `Interned::new_unchecked`, and using iterator `map`/`collect` to precreate region variables and late-bound regions.
Builds common constants (`unit`, `true`, `false`) by interning `ConstData` values via `CtxtInterners::intern_const` through a local `mk_const` closure.
Creates a `TyCtxtFeed` keyed by `()` for feeding unit-keyed queries; it does not call other listed methods.
Creates a `TyCtxtFeed` keyed by `LOCAL_CRATE` for feeding local-crate queries; it does not call other listed methods.
Feeds the `type_of` query for an anonymous const after checking its definition kind with `TyCtxt::def_kind`, then invoking the feed helper’s `type_of` setter.
Returns the stored feed key; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the stored `LocalDefId`; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns a reference to the underlying global context (`gcx`); it does not call other listed methods.
Enters thread-local type-context scope by creating an implicit context with `tls::ImplicitCtxt::new`, installing it with `tls::enter_context`, and then invoking the provided closure `f`.

Returns codegen attributes for body-like definitions by first calling `TyCtxt::def_kind`; if that kind supports codegen attrs it calls `TyCtxt::codegen_fn_attrs`, otherwise it returns the empty attrs for const-like kinds or bugs on unexpected kinds.
Arena-allocates a stealable THIR wrapper by calling `Steal::new` and then `arena.alloc`.
Arena-allocates a stealable MIR body wrapper by calling `Steal::new` and then `arena.alloc`.
Arena-allocates a stealable promoted-body collection by calling `Steal::new` and then `arena.alloc`.
Constructs ADT definition data with `ty::AdtDefData::new` and interns it by calling `TyCtxt::mk_adt_def_from_data`.

Creates an immutable byte allocation with `interpret::Allocation::from_bytes_byte_aligned_immutable`, interns it with `TyCtxt::mk_const_alloc`, and registers it by calling `TyCtxt::reserve_and_set_memory_alloc`.

Reads `rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_{start,end}` attributes for a definition by calling `TyCtxt::get_attr`; the local parser inspects `meta_item_list`/`as_deref`, returns `Bound::Included` for valid integer literals, and reports malformed attributes via `TyCtxt::dcx().span_delayed_bug`.
Attempts to lift a value into the global type context by calling `Lift::lift_to_tcx` on the input.

Builds and returns a fully initialized `GlobalCtxt` by parsing the target data layout, creating interner/common type/lifetime/const tables, cloning profiling state, and initializing caches and allocation state. Calls `parse_data_layout`, `dcx`, `emit_fatal`, `new`, `clone`, and `default`.
Delegates to the session’s optimization hint logic, supplying the local crate name and the provided message thunk. Calls `crate_name`.
Returns the language-items table for the current compilation context by querying it. Calls `get_lang_items`.
Looks up a diagnostic item definition id by symbol name from the global diagnostic-items map. Calls `all_diagnostic_items`.
Looks up the diagnostic item symbol for a definition id from the crate-local diagnostic-items map. Calls `diagnostic_items`.
Checks whether a given definition id is registered under the specified diagnostic-item name in its crate. Calls `diagnostic_items`.
Returns the compiler stability index for the current crate. Calls `stability_index`.
Returns the enabled feature set for the current compilation. Calls `features_query`.

Returns the `DefKey` for a definition by converting the query parameter and dispatching to local definitions storage or the crate store depending on locality. Calls `into_query_param`, `definitions_untracked`, and `cstore_untracked`.
Returns the `DefPath` for a definition by reading from local definitions storage for local ids and from the crate store for external ids. Calls `definitions_untracked` and `cstore_untracked`.
Returns the stable `DefPathHash` for a definition, using local definitions storage for local ids and the crate store for external ids. Calls `definitions_untracked` and `cstore_untracked`.
Returns the stable crate id for a crate number, using the local cached id for `LOCAL_CRATE` and the crate store for upstream crates. Calls `cstore_untracked`.
Maps a stable crate id back to a crate number, returning `LOCAL_CRATE` for the local id and otherwise delegating to the crate store. Calls `stable_crate_id` and `cstore_untracked`.

Resolves a `DefPathHash` to a `DefId`, using local definitions for hashes from the local crate and the crate store for upstream hashes. Calls `stable_crate_id`, `cstore_untracked`, and `stable_crate_id_to_crate_num`.

Builds a human-readable debug string containing the crate name, abbreviated stable crate id, and verbose def path, avoiding query recursion by using direct local or crate-store access. Calls `crate_name`, `stable_crate_id`, `cstore_untracked`, and `def_path`.

Creates a new local definition in a query-tracked context, first recording a dependency on the forever-red node, then creating the def, obtaining a feed for it, and assigning the current span. Calls `create_def`, `feed_local_def_id`, and `def_span`.

Returns an iterator over all local definition ids, tracking the forever-red node, repeatedly reading the current number of definitions so newly created ids are included, and freezing definitions after iteration completes. Calls `read_index` and `freeze`.
Returns the frozen local `DefPathTable`, first recording a dependency on the forever-red node so changes in definition count cause re-execution. Calls `read_index` and `freeze`.

Ensures the HIR crate is loaded before freezing the local definitions table and returning its def-path-hash to def-index map. Calls `ensure`, `hir_crate`, `freeze`, and the underlying `def_path_hash_to_def_index_map`.
Returns an untracked frozen read guard to the crate store by reading `self.untracked.cstore` and remapping the guard to the dyn trait object. Calls `read` and `map`.
Returns a shared reference to the untracked compiler context payload stored in `TyCtxt`.
Returns an untracked read guard for the definitions table by calling `read` on `self.untracked.definitions`.
Looks up a local definition’s source span in the untracked span map and falls back to `DUMMY_SP` if absent. Calls `get` and `unwrap_or`.
Constructs a `StableHashingContext` from the session and untracked state, then invokes the supplied closure with it. Calls `StableHashingContext::new` and the closure `f`.
Serializes the on-disk query result cache if it exists, otherwise returns `Ok(0)`. Calls `as_ref`, `map_or`, and cache `serialize`.
Determines whether the local crate exports generics by scanning crate output types and returning true for `Dylib` or `Rlib`. Calls `share_generics`, `crate_types`, `iter`, and `any`.

Checks whether a region is a diagnosable free region, remaps opaque-type synthetic lifetimes back to their originating function lifetime, computes a named bound region, and marks whether it belongs to a trait impl item. Calls `kind`, `get_id`, `as_local`, `expect_local`, `local_parent`, `def_kind`, `map_rpit_lifetime_to_fn_lifetime`, `item_name`, `opt_hir_node_by_def_id`, and `is_bound_region_in_impl_item`.

Collects `impl Trait` or `dyn Trait` occurrences from a function’s explicit return type HIR, returning an empty vector when no return type node is available. Calls `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `hir`, `fn_decl_by_hir_id`, and `visit_ty`.

If a function returns a local type alias, visits the alias type to collect contained `impl Trait` or `dyn Trait` uses and returns them together with the alias generics span information. Calls `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `hir`, `fn_decl_by_hir_id`, `as_local`, `hir_node_by_def_id`, `alias_ty`, `generics`, `visit_ty`, `is_empty`, and `span_for_lifetime_suggestion`.

Returns whether the given impl item belongs to a trait impl, which makes its bound region unsuitable for certain signature-changing diagnostics. Calls `parent`, `to_def_id`, `impl_trait_ref`, and `is_some`.
Reports whether the target architecture uses strict asm symbol naming, currently by checking whether the architecture string contains `"nvptx"`. Calls `contains`.
Builds the `&'static core::panic::Location<'static>` type used for caller-location intrinsics. Calls `require_lang_item`, `type_of`, `mk_args`, `instantiate`, and `Ty::new_imm_ref`.
Returns the grammatical article and human-readable description for a definition by first querying its kind. Calls `def_kind`, `def_kind_descr_article`, and `def_kind_descr`.
Returns the configured type-length limit from the compiler limits query. Calls `limits`.
Returns the configured recursion limit from the compiler limits query. Calls `limits`.
Returns the configured move-size limit from the compiler limits query. Calls `limits`.
Iterates over all trait definition IDs in the local crate and every upstream crate. Calls `crates` and `traits`, using iterator adapters `once`, `chain`, `iter`, `copied`, and `flat_map`.
Returns the local visibility of a definition by querying `visibility` and asserting the result is local with `expect_local`. Calls `visibility` and `expect_local`.
Returns the HIR origin of a local opaque type by looking up the item and extracting its opaque-ty metadata. Calls `hir`, `expect_item`, and `expect_opaque_ty`.
Trait method contract for attempting to lift a value into the `TyCtxt` arena/lifetime, returning the lifted form on success.

Attempts to lift an interned value into `tcx` by checking whether its pointer is contained in the corresponding interner set and, if so, transmuting it to the target lifetime. For internal type-checking scaffolding it also references `_intern_set_ty_from_interned_ty` and `_type_eq`; at runtime it calls `contains_pointer_to` and `then`.

Attempts to lift an interned list into `tcx`; immediately returns the canonical empty list for empty inputs, otherwise checks membership in the appropriate interner set before transmuting lifetimes. Calls `is_empty`, `List::empty`, `contains_pointer_to`, and `then`.

Computes debug statistics for interned types by iterating over all type interner shards, classifying each non-primitive/non-error type variant, counting inference-flag usage, and formatting the report. Calls `lock_shards`, `keys`, and `intersects`.
Returns a debug-printable wrapper around `TyCtxt` that formats interner statistics when printed; the actual formatting logic is delegated to `DebugStats::fmt`.

Formats detailed interner statistics: it invokes the generated type-stat printer and then prints lengths of the generic-args, region, const-allocation, and layout interners. Calls the generated stats formatter from `sty_debug_print!` and `len` on the interners.
Creates a shallow copy of `InternedInSet` by rewrapping the same interned pointer; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Converts the wrapped interned value pointer into an erased `*const ()` for pointer-based identity; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns a shared reference to the underlying `internee` inside `WithCachedTypeInfo`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Compares two interned cached values by equality of their underlying `internee`, preserving `Borrow` consistency; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Hashes the underlying `internee` so hashing matches the `Borrow` view of the interned cached value; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Borrows the interned `List<T>` as a slice reference; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Compares two interned lists by slice equality, preserving `Borrow<[T]>` consistency; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Hashes the interned list as a slice so hashing matches the borrowed slice view; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Macro-generated borrow helper that returns a shared reference to the wrapped value `self.0`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Macro-generated equality implementation that compares wrapped interned values directly, keeping equality aligned with `Borrow`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Macro-generated hash implementation that hashes the wrapped interned value directly, matching the borrowed view; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Converts a safe function signature into an unsafe function-pointer type after asserting the input signature is safe. It calls `map_bound` to rewrite the bound `FnSig` and `new_fn_ptr` to build the resulting `Ty`.

Checks whether a trait or any of its supertraits may define an associated item with the given name, using unhygienic name filtering plus hygienic identifier comparison. It calls `super_traits_of` from the Methods List.
Returns `true` when a type is an opaque alias whose explicit bounds include a positive `Future` trait bound; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Traverses a trait’s transitive supertraits with a stack and visited set, yielding each reachable trait `DefId` once; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Transforms a closure-like signature whose first input is a tuple of arguments into a normal Rust function signature with the requested unsafety. It calls `mk_fn_sig` to construct the rewritten signature.
Interns a bound `PredicateKind` into a canonical `Predicate` using the type context’s predicate interner; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Reuses an existing predicate if its kind already matches the supplied binder, otherwise creates a new interned predicate. It calls `mk_predicate` from the Methods List when reconstruction is needed.

Builds interned generic arguments from an iterator, and in debug builds verifies the argument count against the target item’s generics, including the inherent associated-type projection adjustment. It calls `mk_args_from_iter` to produce the final `GenericArgsRef`.
Interns a `Const` from its `ConstKind` and type through the context’s const interner; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Interns a `Ty` from a `TyKind` through the context’s type interner; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Constructs a generic argument corresponding to a generic parameter definition by creating the appropriate lifetime, type, or const parameter representation; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Appends a field projection to a MIR place. It calls `mk_place_elem` from the Methods List with `PlaceElem::Field`.
Appends a dereference projection to a MIR place. It calls `mk_place_elem` from the Methods List with `PlaceElem::Deref`.
Appends a named downcast projection for the selected ADT variant to a MIR place. It calls `mk_place_elem` from the Methods List with `PlaceElem::Downcast`.
Appends an unnamed downcast projection for the selected variant to a MIR place. It calls `mk_place_elem` from the Methods List with `PlaceElem::Downcast`.
Appends an index projection to a MIR place. It calls `mk_place_elem` from the Methods List with `PlaceElem::Index`.
Creates a new MIR place by cloning the existing projection list, pushing one more projection element, and interning the resulting projection sequence. It calls `mk_place_elems` from the Methods List.
Validates that existential predicates are non-empty and sorted by stable ordering, then interns the predicate list; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Interns a list of clauses without reordering or deduplicating permutations; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Collects an iterator of consts and produces an interned const list through the generic `CollectAndApply` path. It calls `collect_and_apply` and then `mk_const_list`.
Builds a `ty::FnSig` from input types plus a separate output type, appending the output after the inputs and interning the combined type list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_type_list`.
Collects existential predicates from an iterator and interns them as a list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_poly_existential_predicates`.
Collects clauses from an iterator and interns them into a canonical clause list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_clauses`.
Collects types from an iterator and interns them as a type list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_type_list`.
Collects generic arguments from an iterator and interns them as `GenericArgsRef`. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_args`.
Collects canonical variable infos from an iterator and interns them as a list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_canonical_var_infos`.
Collects MIR place elements from an iterator and interns them as a list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_place_elems`.
Collects field indices from an iterator and interns them as a list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_fields`.
Builds trait generic arguments by prepending the `self` type to the remaining arguments and interning the result. It calls `mk_args_from_iter`.
Collects bound variable kinds from an iterator and interns them as a list. It calls `collect_and_apply` and `mk_bound_variable_kinds`.

Emits a lint for a specific HIR node and span using a `DecorateLint` helper. It gets the message from `msg`, retrieves the level with `lint_level_at_node`, and reports through `struct_lint_level`, invoking `decorate_lint` on the diagnostic.
Constructs a span-based lint diagnostic for a HIR node with an explicit message and decoration closure. It calls `lint_level_at_node` and then `struct_lint_level`.

Emits a lint for a HIR node without an explicit span by delegating to the node-based lint builder. It calls `struct_lint_node`, uses `msg` to obtain the message, and invokes `decorate_lint` in the decoration closure.
Constructs a lint diagnostic for a HIR node without attaching a separate span. It calls `lint_level_at_node` and then `struct_lint_level`.
Looks up the trait candidates in scope for a HIR id by querying the owner’s trait map and indexing by local id. It calls `in_scope_traits_map`.
Returns the resolved named bound variable associated with a HIR id, if present, by consulting the owner’s named-variable map. It calls `named_variable_map`.
Checks whether a HIR id is recorded as a late-bound variable in its owner’s late-bound set. It calls `is_late_bound_map`.

Fetches and interns the late-bound variable kinds for a HIR node, panicking if no entry exists. It calls `late_bound_vars_map` to retrieve the raw data and `mk_bound_variable_kinds` to intern it; on the error path it also uses `hir` and `node_to_string` for the bug message.

Determines whether a function is usable as `const`, including feature-gate checks for const-unstable items. It calls `is_const_fn_raw`, `lookup_const_stability`, and, for unstable const items, inspects `features().declared_lib_features.iter().any(...)`.
Checks whether a local impl is a const trait impl by inspecting its HIR generics for a host-effect const parameter. It calls `as_local` and `hir_node_by_def_id`.
Converts a `LocalDefId` to its `HirId`, assuming the mapping exists. It calls `opt_local_def_id_to_hir_id` and unwraps the result.
Reports whether the next trait solver is enabled globally in unstable options by reading the session setting via `map_or`.
Reports whether the next trait solver is enabled for coherence checking in unstable options by reading the session setting via `map_or`.
Checks whether a definition corresponds to impl-trait-in-trait by testing for RPITIT metadata. It calls `opt_rpitit_info`.
Returns the locally resolved children of a module, or an empty slice if none were recorded. It calls `resolutions`.

Registers query providers backed by resolver and untracked context data, including trait-import data, glob imports, extern crate mappings, crate attributes, panic-handler presence, and source spans. The closures call `resolutions`, `alloc`, `hir`, `krate_attrs`, `lang_items`, `panic_impl`, and use helpers such as `contains_name`, `is_some_and`, `is_local`, and `unwrap_or`.
Returns whether the given mutability is mutable by directly calling `is_mut` on the `Mutability` value.
Checks whether a generator is async by calling `generator_kind(def_id)` and matching the result against `Some(hir::GeneratorKind::Async(_))`.

Returns the concrete return type and output span for a local function-like item or closure whose erased return type is `impl Trait`. It first calls `hir().get_by_def_id` to restrict accepted HIR nodes, then calls `type_of(scope_def_id)` and `instantiate_identity` to obtain the item type. If `kind` shows a `FnDef`, it calls `fn_sig`, `erase_late_bound_regions`, and `output`, checks `is_impl_trait`, and then calls `hir().local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `hir().fn_decl_by_hir_id`, and `span` to produce the `(Ty, Span)` result; otherwise it returns `None`.

Constructs a `ty::AliasTy` for the given definition by first calling `check_and_mk_args(def_id, args)` to validate and intern the generic arguments, then returning the alias with that `def_id` and computed `args`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Trait requirement for constructing an early-bound lifetime mapping from a generic parameter; no concrete intra-file method calls are present in this declaration.
Trait requirement for constructing a late-bound lifetime mapping from an index and generic parameter; no concrete intra-file method calls are present in this declaration.
Trait requirement for extracting the underlying definition id from a resolved lifetime argument; no concrete intra-file method calls are present in this declaration.
Trait requirement for shifting a resolved lifetime argument by a binder depth amount; no concrete intra-file method calls are present in this declaration.
Builds an early-bound `ResolvedArg` for the given generic parameter and returns it with the local def id. It calls `to_def_id` to convert the parameter def id into the `EarlyBound` form.

Builds a late-bound `ResolvedArg` at `INNERMOST` depth for the given index and generic parameter, returning it with the local def id. It calls `to_def_id` to convert the parameter def id for the `LateBound` result.
Returns the `DefId` carried by early-bound, late-bound, or free resolved arguments, and `None` for static or error lifetimes. It does not call other methods from the provided methods list.
Shifts the De Bruijn depth of a late-bound resolved argument and leaves all other variants unchanged. It calls `shifted_in` when the argument is `LateBound`.
Formats each `Scope` variant in a truncated debug form that omits recursive scope tails; it calls the formatter builder methods `debug_struct`, `field`, and `finish`.

Registers this module's query providers, wiring `resolve_bound_vars`, `is_late_bound_map`, `object_lifetime_default`, and closure-based accessors for stored maps; the accessors call `tcx.resolve_bound_vars(id)` and then `get` on the resulting maps.

Builds the `ResolveBoundVars` result for one HIR owner by creating a `BoundVarContext`, dispatching to the matching visitor entry point, and then copying collected definitions into owner-indexed maps. It calls `hir_owner_node`, then one of `visit_item`, `visit_foreign_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_impl_item`, and finally uses `entry`, `or_default`, and `insert` to populate the result.

Walks outward through the current scope stack to determine the binder variables and binder composition mode for a nested poly-trait-ref, including concatenating enclosing binder vars with supertrait vars when needed. It calls `clone`, `is_empty`, `dcx`, `delayed_bug`, `entry`, `or_default`, and `extend`.

Processes a poly trait reference by computing enclosing binder context, creating late-bound entries for its bound generic parameters, optionally rejecting non-lifetime binders, recording the resulting binder list, and visiting the trait ref inside a new binder scope. Visits a nested body within a `Body` scope so inner references resolve with the body boundary in place. It calls `hir`, `body`, `with`, `id`, and `visit_body`.

Handles closure expressions specially: it diagnoses inferred types inside `for<>` closures, builds late-bound vars for closure binders, rejects non-region late-bound params, records the binders, and then visits the closure within a new binder scope; non-closure expressions are walked normally. Local helper for `visit_expr` that searches a type for an inferred `_` and returns its span if found. It calls the nested visitor's `visit_ty` and then `break_value` on the control-flow result.
Searches a type subtree for the first inferred type and stores its span, otherwise continues traversal. It calls `is_some` to stop after a hit and `walk_ty` to recurse into nested types.

Handles foreign items by using `visit_early_late` for foreign functions and otherwise just walking foreign statics and types. It calls `visit_early_late` and `walk_foreign_item`.

Resolves bindings inside types, with special handling for bare function types, trait objects, explicit lifetime parameters, references, and opaque defs. Handles trait items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. Handles impl items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_impl_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, and `visit_ty`.

Resolves a lifetime reference according to its kind: inserts `'static`, resolves named lifetime params, and ignores error or inference/default placeholders for later stages. It calls `insert_lifetime` for `Static` and `resolve_lifetime_ref` for `Param`.

Visits each path segment's generic arguments with the correct depth and resolves paths that refer to type or const parameters. It calls `visit_segment_args` for segment arguments and `resolve_type_ref` on type/const parameter paths.

Processes a function-like item by extracting the output type, copying inferred-delegation late-bound vars when present, applying lifetime elision analysis, walking the function signature/kind, and then visiting the body. It calls `fn_sig`, `skip_binder`, `bound_vars`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `visit_fn_like_elision`, `walk_fn_kind`, and `visit_nested_body`.
Visits generic parameters and where predicates inside a trait-ref-boundary scope so nested trait refs are resolved with the proper boundary. It calls `with`.

Handles parameter bounds, adding a binder scope for `LangItemTrait` bounds before visiting their contents, while ordinary bounds are traversed directly. Visits a poly trait ref using the general inner handler with non-lifetime binders allowed; it calls `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`.
Visits an anonymous const under a late-boundary scope so late-bound regions cannot escape into constants. It calls `with` and `walk_anon_const`.

Computes the object lifetime default for a type parameter by inspecting its HIR generics and collecting direct `T: 'a` outlives bounds. Creates a nested `BoundVarContext` with a replacement scope and executes a callback inside that scope. It enters a debug span with `enter` and then invokes the provided closure `f`.
Stores the late-bound variable binder list for a HIR node in the output map and rejects accidental overwrites. It updates the map with `insert`.

Builds a binder scope where lifetime params may be early- or late-bound depending on `tcx.is_late_bound`, records the resulting late-bound binder kinds, and visits the nested item in that scope. Resolves a lifetime reference by walking outward through the scope stack, tracking De Bruijn depth, root generics, binder entries, body ownership, and late-bound capture barriers to classify the reference as early-bound, late-bound, free, error, or unresolved. Resolves a type or const generic parameter reference by walking outward through scopes, tracking binder depth and late-bound capture barriers, and classifying the reference as early-bound, late-bound, or unresolved/error. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, and `shifted` during lookup, and emits capture diagnostics with `emit_err` before recording the final result with `insert`.

Visits generic arguments on a path segment, resolving explicit lifetimes first, handling paren-sugar function traits specially, and computing object-lifetime-default scopes for type arguments based on the referenced item and surrounding context. It explicitly calls `visit_fn_like_elision` for paren-sugar segments, `visit_lifetime` for lifetime args, `object_lifetime_default` to compute defaults for type parameters, `with` to enter object-default scopes, `visit_ty` for type args, `visit_anon_const` for const args, `visit_id` for inferred args, and `supertrait_hrtb_vars` when collecting higher-ranked vars from supertraits.

Searches a trait/supertrait graph for an associated item with the given name and kind, accumulating higher-ranked bound variables introduced by traversed supertrait predicates. It queries associated items with `associated_items`/`find_by_name_and_kind`, fetches relevant supertrait predicates with `super_predicates_that_define_assoc_item`, and extends the traversal stack with collected obligations.

Visits function-like input/output types under an object-lifetime-default scope that supplies `'static` for elided trait-object lifetimes, except that closure outputs are visited outside that scope. It calls `with` to install the defaulting scope and `visit_ty` to traverse input and output types.

Resolves an elided object lifetime by scanning outward for the nearest applicable object-lifetime-default scope, adjusting for intervening binders, and defaulting to `'static` at the root. It calls `insert_lifetime` to record the chosen lifetime after applying `shifted`.
Records the resolved lifetime for a lifetime HIR node in the output map. It updates the definitions table with `insert`.

Removes a previously inserted lifetime mapping when later validation determines that the resolution was erroneous, asserting that the removed value matches the expected bad definition. It removes the entry with `swap_remove`.

Computes the set of lifetime parameters in a function owner that should be treated as late-bound by comparing where each lifetime appears in inputs, outputs, and where-clauses, while excluding lifetimes constrained through type aliases after lowering. It drives analysis by calling HIR accessors such as `fn_decl_by_hir_id` and `get_generics`, invokes the nested collectors via `visit_ty`, `walk_fn_ret_ty`, and `visit_generics`, and finally allocates the resulting set with `alloc`.

Marks parameter types as constrained, skips descending into projection or inherent aliases, and otherwise continues recursive type traversal. It calls `kind` to inspect the type and `super_visit_with` to visit nested structure when traversal continues.
Ignores constants for constrained-argument collection and immediately continues traversal. It does not call other methods from the provided methods list.
Marks early-bound regions as constrained and otherwise leaves region handling unchanged. It calls `kind` to inspect the region kind.

Traverses HIR types to collect only those lifetime occurrences that contribute to input constraints, skipping associated type projections and selectively recursing into type-alias arguments based on a lowered-type constraint analysis. It calls the nested post-lowering visitor's `visit_ty`, visits constrained alias args with `visit_generic_arg`, traverses plain path segments with `visit_path_segment`, and falls back to `walk_ty` for ordinary recursive HIR traversal.
Collects named lifetime parameters encountered by the constrained-input visitor into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.
Collects every named lifetime parameter encountered during traversal into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.

Rejects late-bound type or const parameters in a binder, emitting either an immediate feature-gated error or a delayed bug, and rewrites their recorded resolution to `Error`. Builds the canonical `ty::Generics` for a local definition by analyzing its HIR kind and parent context, with special handling for RPITITs, delegation, nested items, anon consts, const defaults, const blocks, closures, and opaque types. Helper for function-like signatures that first checks generic lifetime parameters for `tcx.is_late_bound`, then traverses the function declaration with `LateBoundRegionsDetector` and returns any recorded span. It calls `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_ty@445-457`, `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_poly_trait_ref@459-466`, and `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_lifetime@468-486` indirectly via `visitor.visit_fn_decl(decl)`.

Visits a type while searching for late-bound regions, adjusting the Debruijn depth when entering bare function types and otherwise recursively traversing the type. It calls `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_ty@445-457` recursively through `intravisit::walk_ty`.

Visits a poly trait reference while searching for late-bound regions, increasing the Debruijn depth for the binder and then recursively walking the trait reference. It calls `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_poly_trait_ref@459-466` recursively through `intravisit::walk_poly_trait_ref`.

Examines a lifetime occurrence and marks an error span when it resolves to an unexpected late-bound, free, erroneous, or unresolved lifetime outside the currently permitted binder depth. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Helper for function-like signatures that first checks generic lifetime parameters for `tcx.is_late_bound`, then traverses the function declaration with `LateBoundRegionsDetector` and returns any recorded span. It calls `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_ty@445-457`, `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_poly_trait_ref@459-466`, and `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_lifetime@468-486` indirectly via `visitor.visit_fn_decl(decl)`.

Visits a generic parameter and, for const parameters, temporarily marks that traversal is inside a parameter type before visiting the const parameter's type. It may call methods of the visitor during `visit_ty`, but does not directly call another listed method.

Detects whether the target anonymous const occurs inside a const parameter type and otherwise keeps traversing nested anonymous const structure. It calls `impl<'v> Visitor<'v> for AnonConstInParamTyDetector::visit_anon_const@531-537` recursively through `intravisit::walk_anon_const`.

For impls, it returns direct impl members and, when the impl implements a trait, likewise appends impl-side synthesized RPITIT associated types by calling `associated_types_for_impl_traits_in_associated_fn` for each impl function.

Builds a `ty::AssocItems` collection for a trait or impl. It returns an empty collection for trait aliases; otherwise it calls `associated_item_def_ids` to enumerate item ids and calls `associated_item` to materialize each `ty::AssocItem`.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/assoc.rs::as: Reconstructs a single `ty::AssocItem` for a local trait or impl member by inspecting its HIR parent and searching that parent’s item list. It calls `associated_item_from_impl_item_ref` when the parent is an impl and `associated_item_from_trait_item_ref` when the parent is a trait; otherwise it reports a compiler bug.

Converts a HIR `TraitItemRef` into a `ty::AssocItem`, deriving the associated kind, self-parameter flag, trait container, and setting both `def_id` and `trait_item_def_id` to the trait item’s `DefId`.
Converts a HIR `ImplItemRef` into a `ty::AssocItem`, deriving the associated kind, self-parameter flag, impl container, and preserving any linked `trait_item_def_id` from the impl item.

Computes synthesized associated type `DefId`s for return-position `impl Trait` appearing in an associated function. For trait methods, it visits the return type to collect opaque types and calls `associated_type_for_impl_trait_in_trait` for each one. For impl methods, it calls `associated_item` to find the implemented trait method, recursively calls `associated_types_for_impl_traits_in_associated_fn` on that trait method, and then calls `associated_type_for_impl_trait_in_impl` to mirror each trait-side synthesized associated type into the impl.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/assoc.rs::im: Traverses a type subtree while collecting unique opaque return types used for RPITIT lowering. When it encounters a new opaque type, it looks up the opaque item and calls `walk_param_bound` on its bounds, then calls `walk_ty` to continue recursive traversal.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/assoc.rs::as: Synthesizes a trait-side associated type definition for an opaque return type in a trait method. It validates the opaque origin, creates a new associated type `DefId`, records RPITIT metadata in its associated item, and copies or adapts visibility, defaultness, type information, generics, and inferred outlives from the original opaque and containing trait method. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Synthesizes an impl-side associated type corresponding to a trait-side RPITIT associated type for a particular impl method. It creates a new impl associated type `DefId`, records the link back to `trait_assoc_def_id`, and copies or adapts span, visibility, defaultness, generics, and inferred outlives for the impl context. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Builds the full predicate set for a definition by starting from `tcx.predicates_defined_on(def_id)` and, for trait definitions, appending the implicit `Self: Trait` predicate via `ty::TraitRef::identity(...).upcast(...)`.

Collects explicit predicates written on a local item, with special inheritance/rebasing paths for RPITITs and normal HIR lowering otherwise. For RPITIT trait items, it calls `tcx.explicit_predicates_of(...)` to inherit parent function predicates and `compute_bidirectional_outlives_predicates(...)` to add duplicated lifetime equalities. For RPITIT impl items, it calls `tcx.explicit_predicates_of(...)` again and rebases those trait associated-item predicates onto the impl. In the general path, it lowers item generics, bounds, implicit `Sized`/const-arg predicates, and default-impl/delegation-related predicates into `ty::GenericPredicates`.

Adds paired outlives predicates equating each duplicated opaque lifetime parameter with its original parent lifetime. It calls `tcx.map_opaque_lifetime_to_parent_lifetime(...)` to find the original lifetime and pushes two `RegionOutlives` clauses for both directions.

Traverses the HIR for an item to collect `ConstEvaluatable` predicates for unevaluated anonymous consts appearing in impl headers, generics, and function signatures. It drives the visitor by calling `visit_trait_ref(...)`, `visit_ty(...)`, `visit_generics(...)`, and `visit_fn_decl(...)`, while relying on `visit_anon_const(...)` to record predicates and `visit_const_param_default(...)` to skip const parameter defaults.

Visitor hook that turns an unevaluated anonymous const into a `ConstEvaluatable` clause. It calls `ty::Const::from_anon_const(...)` to lower the const and inserts the predicate when the resulting const kind is unevaluated.
Visitor hook that intentionally ignores const parameter defaults so they are checked only when instantiated; it does not call any other methods in this file.
Trait-only wrapper that asserts the definition is a trait and then calls `gather_explicit_predicates_of(...)` to collect its explicit predicates and bounds.

Computes the user-visible explicit predicates for a local item. For traits, it calls `trait_explicit_predicates_and_bounds(...)` and filters out associated-type bounds that should instead be reported through item bounds. For other items, it ultimately calls `gather_explicit_predicates_of(...)`, with extra handling to inherit predicates for anon const defaults and to append const-parameter type predicates where needed.
Returns only the immediate supertrait predicates for a trait by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::SelfOnly`.
Returns supertrait predicates whose `Self` bounds may define a named associated item by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::SelfThatDefines(assoc_name)`.

Computes the implied predicates for a trait or trait alias by calling `implied_predicates_with_filter(...)` with `PredicateFilter::All` for trait aliases and `PredicateFilter::SelfAndAssociatedTypeBounds` for ordinary traits.

Lowers a trait’s supertrait list and matching where-clause bounds into implied predicates according to the requested filter. For external traits it calls `tcx.super_predicates_of(...)`; for local traits it calls `icx.lowerer().lower_mono_bounds(...)` and `icx.probe_ty_param_bounds_in_generics(...)` to gather bounds, then recursively forces `tcx.super_predicates_of(...)` or `tcx.implied_predicates_of(...)` on positive trait bounds to detect cycles and elaborate nested associated-type bounds.

Collects predicates relevant to a specific type parameter within an item, including inherited parent bounds, local where-clause bounds, and the implicit `Self: Trait` bound for trait `Self`. It calls `ItemCtxt::probe_ty_param_bounds(...)` on the parent when needed and `ItemCtxt::probe_ty_param_bounds_in_generics(...)` on the current item, then filters the result to trait predicates whose self type is the target parameter.

Collects lowered predicate clauses for a specific type parameter from the HIR generics where-clause, honoring the requested `PredicateFilter` to keep all bounds, only `Self` bounds, or only `Self` bounds that define a particular associated item. It iterates bound predicates, chooses the bounded type either from the target parameter or by lowering the predicate’s explicit bounded type, lowers matching bounds into a `Bounds` accumulator, and returns the accumulated clauses with spans. This method explicitly calls `is_param_bound`, `to_def_id`, `to_ty`, `late_bound_vars`, `astconv`, `add_bounds`, `map_or`, `bound_defines_assoc_item`, and `clauses`.

Checks whether a trait bound could define a particular associated item name. It calls `trait_ref.trait_def_id()` to resolve the bound’s trait and then `self.tcx.trait_may_define_assoc_item(...)` to test that trait.

Classifies a lifetime by querying `get_lifetime_res`, then records it only if it is free with respect to `current_binders` or is a special always-collectable case like `'static`/error. It uses `contains` to avoid locally bound or duplicate entries and `push` to store newly collected lifetimes; unexpected resolutions trigger a compiler bug.
Expands an elided-lifetime anchor resolved from `get_lifetime_res` into synthesized underscore `Lifetime` values and calls `record_lifetime_use` for each generated lifetime.
Handles an explicit lifetime node by calling `record_lifetime_use` to classify and collect it if appropriate.
Visits a path segment by first calling `record_elided_anchor` to collect any elided lifetimes attached to the segment, then delegating to `walk_path_segment` to recurse into the segment contents.

Visits a higher-ranked trait reference by pushing its binder onto the current binder stack, calling `walk_poly_trait_ref` to traverse nested nodes under that binding scope, and then popping the binder.

Visits a type while managing binding scopes and elided references: for bare function types it pushes a binder, calls `walk_ty`, then pops it; for `TyKind::Ref(None, _)` it calls `record_elided_anchor` before `walk_ty`; otherwise it just calls `walk_ty`.

Creates a `LifetimeCollectVisitor`, calls `LifetimeCollectVisitor::new` to initialize it, then calls `visit_fn_ret_ty` to walk the function return type and collect referenced lifetimes, finally returning the collected lifetimes.

Collects free lifetimes appearing in a `GenericBounds` list by creating a visitor with `LifetimeCollectVisitor::new`, calling `visit_param_bound` for each bound, and returning the visitor’s collected lifetimes.

Delegates lifetime uses directly to the lifetime resolver. It explicitly calls `LateResolutionVisitor::resolve_lifetime`.
Resolves a generics block by visiting its generic parameters and then each where-clause predicate. It explicitly calls `visit_generic_params` and `visit_where_predicate`.
Resolves a closure binder; it does nothing for `NotPresent` and, for `for<...>` binders, visits the binder's generic parameters. It explicitly calls `visit_generic_params`.

Resolves a generic argument while marking that generic arguments are being processed. For type arguments, it may reinterpret a trivial path type as a const argument by probing lexical resolution with `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, then resolving it inside `resolve_anon_const_manual` via `smart_resolve_path` and `visit_path`; otherwise it visits the type with `visit_ty`. For lifetime arguments it calls `visit_lifetime`, and for const arguments it calls `resolve_anon_const`.

Resolves an associated-item constraint by visiting its identifier, optional generic arguments, and constraint body. It explicitly calls `visit_ident`, wraps generic arguments in `with_lifetime_rib` before calling `visit_generic_args`, uses `visit_ty` or `resolve_anon_const` for equality terms, and calls `record_lifetime_params_for_impl_trait` for bound constraints.

Resolves generic arguments attached to a path segment. For angle-bracketed arguments it delegates to `visit::walk_generic_args`; for parenthesized arguments it inspects lifetime ribs and either introduces an anonymous-lifetime rib with `with_lifetime_rib` and resolves the function-like signature via `resolve_fn_signature`, or falls back to `visit::walk_generic_args`.

Resolves a where-clause predicate while tracking it in diagnostic metadata and forbidding anonymous lifetimes by default. For bound predicates it enters `with_lifetime_rib`, then `with_generic_param_rib`, and explicitly calls `visit_generic_params`, `visit_ty`, and `visit_param_bound`; otherwise it falls back to `visit::walk_where_predicate`.

Resolves names inside an inline assembly block by walking each operand. It explicitly calls `visit_expr` for input/output expressions, `resolve_anon_const` for const operands, `visit_inline_asm_sym` for symbol operands, and `visit_block` for label operands.

Resolves an inline-asm symbol path inside dedicated value, type, and label ribs so surrounding bindings are blocked like anon-const resolution. It explicitly nests `with_rib` and `with_label_rib`, then calls `smart_resolve_path` and `visit::walk_inline_asm_sym`.
Resolves documentation links attached to an enum variant and then walks the variant body. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` and `visit::walk_variant`.
Resolves an enum variant discriminant as an anonymous const in enum-discriminant context. It explicitly calls `resolve_anon_const`.
Resolves documentation links attached to a field definition and then walks the field. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` and `visit::walk_field_def`.

Constructs a late-resolution visitor rooted at the crate graph root, initializing parent scope, namespace ribs, label and lifetime stacks, and diagnostic state. It explicitly calls `ParentScope::module`, `Rib::new`, and `Default::default`.
Attempts lexical-scope resolution of an identifier in a namespace without finalization or ignored bindings. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`.
Resolves an identifier in the current lexical scope with configurable finalization and optional binding suppression. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`.
Resolves a path against the current parent scope and rib stacks, optionally in a specific namespace and finalize mode. It explicitly calls `Resolver::resolve_path_with_ribs`.
Runs a closure inside a temporary namespace rib, pushing a new rib before execution and popping it afterward. It explicitly calls `Rib::new` around the provided `work` closure.

Executes work in the module scope for a node when that node defines a module, temporarily switching `parent_scope.module` and pushing module ribs for both value and type namespaces. It explicitly calls `get_module`, `replace`, `with_rib`, and then the supplied closure `f`.

Resolves generic parameter declarations while enforcing forward-reference bans for later type/const parameters and optionally `Self` in ADT defaults. Inside `with_lifetime_rib`, it explicitly calls `visit_param_bound` for bounds, `visit_ty` for type defaults, and `resolve_anon_const` for const defaults, while pushing and removing temporary ban ribs as parameters become available.
Runs a closure inside a temporary lifetime rib, saving and restoring lifetime-elision candidates around the work. It explicitly calls `LifetimeRib::new` around the provided `work` closure.

Resolves a named or anonymous lifetime use by handling `'static`, delegating `_` to `resolve_anonymous_lifetime`, and otherwise searching lifetime ribs from innermost to outermost. On success it explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res`; on special error cases it emits diagnostics such as forbidden non-static or undeclared lifetime errors.

Resolves an underscore or elided lifetime according to the active lifetime ribs. It may create a fresh lifetime with `create_fresh_lifetime` and record it with `record_lifetime_res`, emit lints or errors for forbidden anonymous lifetimes, accumulate elision failures, or report missing lifetime specifiers via `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers`.

Creates a synthetic underscore lifetime for an elided lifetime position, records an anchor range for it, and resolves it as an anonymous lifetime. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res` and `resolve_anonymous_lifetime`.
Allocates a fresh synthetic lifetime parameter for an anonymous lifetime, records it, and stores it for later HIR lowering. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_param`.

Resolves omitted lifetime arguments in path segments that refer to lifetime-parameterized types or traits. It explicitly calls `record_lifetime_res` to create anchor and inferred entries; depending on context it may call `create_fresh_lifetime`, emit diagnostics, buffer lints, or call `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers` when explicit lifetimes are required.

Records the resolved meaning of a lifetime node, panicking if the node was already resolved, and tracks elision candidates for named, fresh, or static lifetimes. It updates the resolution map directly and does not call other listed methods.
Records the resolved meaning of a lifetime parameter node, panicking on duplicate resolution. It updates the resolution map directly and does not call other listed methods.

Resolves the lifetimes of a function signature by first resolving parameter patterns and types, then resolving the return type under the appropriate elision rib, and finally reporting elision failures if needed. It explicitly calls `resolve_fn_params`, wraps return-type traversal in `with_lifetime_rib`, and may call `report_missing_lifetime_specifiers`.

Resolves function parameter patterns and types while computing the lifetime elision candidate for the signature. For each parameter it explicitly calls `with_lifetime_rib` to resolve patterns via `resolve_pattern`, then calls `visit_ty` to collect lifetime candidates, and finally uses `find_lifetime_for_self` when `self`-based elision may apply.

Searches a type for references of the form `&'a Self` (including implicit/desugared self forms) to identify elision candidates tied to `self`. It builds a local visitor whose `visit_ty` logic uses `is_self_ty`, then walks the type to collect matching lifetime resolutions.

Checks whether a type denotes `Self`, either as implicit self, an explicit self type parameter/alias, or the current impl self type. It reads the path resolution via `full_res` and performs no calls to other listed methods.

Visits a type while detecting `&Self` references and recording the resolved lifetime used by that reference; when the referenced inner type is `Self`, it uses `is_self_ty` and stores the lifetime resolution, then calls `visit::walk_ty` to continue traversing nested type structure.
Overrides expression visiting as a no-op so this visitor only inspects types and does not recurse into expressions.

Resolves a loop/block label by searching label ribs from innermost to outermost, adjusting macro-generated labels when crossing `MacroDefinition` ribs, and returning either the matching label or an error. It explicitly calls `is_label_valid_from_rib` to reject labels hidden behind barriers and `suggestion_for_label_in_rib` to collect typo suggestions.
Checks whether a resolved label is reachable from the current scope by scanning intervening label ribs for barriers. It explicitly calls `is_label_barrier` on each rib kind.

Resolves an enum/struct/union item by installing the current self item, generic-parameter scopes, and a `Self` type alias for the ADT, then traversing the item body. It explicitly calls `with_current_self_item`, `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_self_rib`, and `visit::walk_item`.

Checks `use` trees for imports that incorrectly refer to local variables or type parameters, emitting future-proofing diagnostics for such lexical-scope captures. For each relevant namespace it explicitly calls `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, may call `resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` to probe through an item binding, and recursively calls `future_proof_import` on nested imports.

Dispatches late resolution for each item kind, setting up the appropriate ribs, doc-link handling, and specialized resolution flow. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` for most items, `with_generic_param_rib` plus `visit::walk_item` for type aliases and functions, `resolve_adt` for enums/structs/unions, `resolve_implementation` for impls, `with_self_rib`, `visit_generics`, and `resolve_trait_items` for traits, `with_scope` for trait aliases, `with_static_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `visit_ty`, and `resolve_const_body` for statics/consts, and `future_proof_import` for nested-use imports.

Creates temporary type, value, and lifetime ribs for generic parameters, records their bindings, checks for duplicate names and lifetime shadowing, runs a nested resolution action, then tears the ribs down and reports lifetime uses. It explicitly calls `Rib::new`, `signal_lifetime_shadowing`, `record_lifetime_param`, `report_error`, `record_partial_res`, and `maybe_report_lifetime_uses`.
Pushes a new label rib for the duration of a closure and then pops it afterward. It explicitly calls `Rib::new` before executing the nested action.
Creates item-style ribs in both value and type namespaces for resolving a static item body. It explicitly calls `with_rib` twice, nesting the `TypeNS` rib inside the `ValueNS` rib.

Establishes the restricted scope used while resolving const contexts, including value/type ribs, label restrictions, and optional lifetime restrictions for anon consts. It explicitly calls `with_rib` for `ValueNS` and `TypeNS`, uses `force_yes_if` to relax generic usage for repeat expressions, calls `with_label_rib` for label scoping, and conditionally calls `with_lifetime_rib` when generics are forbidden.
Temporarily records the current `Self` type in diagnostic metadata while running a nested action, restoring the previous value afterward.
Temporarily records the current self item id in diagnostic metadata while running a nested action, then restores the previous value.

Resolves all associated items of a trait, setting current-trait metadata and installing per-item generic/lifetime scopes as needed. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links` for each item; for most associated items it uses `with_generic_param_rib` and `visit::walk_assoc_item`, while associated consts additionally call `visit_generics`, `visit_ty`, and `resolve_const_body`, delegations call `resolve_delegation`, and associated types may call `with_lifetime_rib` before walking.

Temporarily resolves and installs the trait reference for an impl, making both the trait module and resolved trait `DefId` available to nested resolution. It explicitly calls `smart_resolve_path_fragment` to resolve the trait path, `expect_full_res` and `opt_def_id` to extract the result, `expect_module` to store the trait module, and then invokes the nested closure.
Pushes a temporary rib in the given namespace containing a `Self` binding, runs a nested action, and then removes the rib. It explicitly calls `Rib::new` to create the scope frame.
Convenience wrapper that installs a `Self` binding in the type namespace. It explicitly calls `with_self_rib_ns` with `TypeNS`.

Resolves an `impl` block by installing generic and lifetime scopes, resolving the optional trait reference, setting up `Self` bindings for the impl type and constructor namespace, recording trait-impl relationships, and then resolving the impl contents. It explicitly calls `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_self_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `with_optional_trait_ref`, `resolve_doc_links`, `walk_trait_ref`, `visit_ty`, `visit_generics`, `with_current_self_type`, `with_self_rib_ns`, and `resolve_impl_item`.

Resolves an associated item inside an impl, enforcing trait-membership checks when the impl targets a trait and using item-specific generic/lifetime scopes. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links`; for associated consts it calls `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `check_trait_item`, `visit_generics`, `visit_ty`, and `resolve_const_body`; for methods and associated types it uses `with_generic_param_rib`, `check_trait_item`, and `visit::walk_assoc_item`; and for delegations it calls `resolve_delegation`.

Validates that an impl associated item corresponds to an item in the currently referenced trait, records its resolution and visibility, reports missing or duplicate matches, and checks namespace/kind consistency. It explicitly calls `find_similarly_named_assoc_item` to build diagnostics, `report_error` to emit trait-membership errors, and `record_partial_res` to store the resolved trait item.

Resolves function parameters by first resolving parameter patterns under an elided-lifetime rib and then resolving each parameter type. It explicitly calls `with_lifetime_rib`, `resolve_pattern`, and `visit_ty`.
Resolves a local `let` binding by visiting its optional type, initializer, optional `else` block, and finally its pattern. It explicitly calls `visit_expr`, `visit_block`, and `resolve_pattern_top`.

Builds a map from pattern identifiers to their binding annotations by walking the pattern tree. It calls `pat.walk` to traverse subpatterns, uses `self.is_base_res_local` to decide whether identifier patterns are true bindings, and for each `PatKind::Or` calls `self.check_consistent_bindings` before merging the returned binding maps into the result.
Checks whether a pattern node’s already-recorded base resolution is a local binding by reading `partial_res_map` and testing for `Res::Local`.

Quickly scans a pattern for or-pattern or never-pattern structure and, if found, triggers full binding-consistency checking. It explicitly calls `compute_and_check_binding_map` when deeper validation is needed.

Traverses a pattern looking for top-level nested or-patterns and validates each one’s bindings. It calls `pat.walk` for traversal and invokes `self.check_consistent_bindings` on every `PatKind::Or` encountered.
Resolves a match arm inside a fresh value rib, including its pattern, optional guard, and body. It explicitly calls `with_rib` and `resolve_pattern_top`.
Creates the top-level binding context for a pattern and resolves it. It explicitly calls `resolve_pattern`.

Resolves a pattern in three ordered phases: first walks the pattern with `walk_pat` so literals and substructure are seen before bindings are introduced, then delegates binding/path resolution to `resolve_pattern_inner`, and finally calls `check_consistent_bindings` to validate variant/binding consistency after resolution.

Performs the direct resolution work for each subpattern by walking it recursively, resolving identifier patterns as existing non-bindings via `try_resolve_as_non_binding` or creating new locals via `fresh_binding`, recording partial results, and resolving tuple-struct/path/struct patterns through `smart_resolve_path`; it also manages temporary binding contexts for or-pattern branches.

Creates or reuses a local pattern binding after normalizing the identifier, detecting duplicate bindings across product and or-pattern contexts, reporting duplicate-binding diagnostics through `report_error`, and accessing the current scope via `innermost_rib_bindings` to either reuse an existing or-pattern binding or insert a fresh `Res::Local`.
Returns the mutable binding map for the innermost rib of the requested namespace.

Attempts to interpret an identifier pattern as an already-existing value-space entity instead of a fresh binding by querying `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, preserving usable constant/unit-ctor resolutions in syntactically ambiguous cases, recording uses when needed, and emitting shadowing/invalid-pattern diagnostics through `report_error` for resolutions that should not be silently rebound.
Convenience wrapper that resolves an AST path by converting it to segments and delegating to `smart_resolve_path_fragment` with finalization and partial-resolution recording enabled.

Core path-resolution routine that selects the namespace from the path source, resolves the path while handling qself/type-relative cases, defers or records partial results, and synthesizes rich use-site diagnostics; within this logic it calls `should_report_errs`, `smart_resolve_report_errors`, `suggest_adding_generic_parameter`, `append_result`, and `resolve_qpath_anywhere`.
Helper that merges a successful `Vec` result into another by appending with `append`, or propagates the first encountered error.
Checks whether `Self` is currently resolvable in the type namespace by calling `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` on `Self` and rejecting `Res::Err`.
Checks whether `self` is currently resolvable in the value namespace by calling `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` on a span-tagged `self` identifier and rejecting `Res::Err`.
Reports a resolution error to the underlying resolver only when `should_report_errs` allows diagnostics in the current context.
Returns whether late resolution should emit diagnostics, suppressing them inside rustdoc function bodies and after a global resolution error already exists.

Tries to resolve a qualified path across multiple namespaces by repeatedly calling `resolve_qpath` for the primary, type, and value namespaces, and if unresolved and not type-qualified, falls back to macro lookup before returning the best partial result.

Resolves a possibly type-qualified path, handling `<T>::...` and `<T as Trait>::...` forms specially by calling `smart_resolve_path_fragment` to validate the trait and trait-item prefixes, then producing a partial result that leaves remaining associated segments for type checking or delegates normal path lookup to the lower-level resolver.

Executes a closure in a scope where an optional loop/block label has been registered: it tracks unused labels, checks for prior definitions via `resolve_label`, emits shadowing diagnostics, and introduces the binding with `with_label_rib` before invoking the closure.
Resolves a labeled block by wrapping `visit_block` inside `with_resolved_label` so the block body sees the label binding.

Resolves a block by pushing the appropriate value/type ribs for anonymous modules or normal lexical scope, tracking macro-definition ribs for nested `macro_rules!`, adjusting bare-struct-literal diagnostic state, visiting each statement with `visit_stmt`, and then restoring the prior module and rib stacks.
Resolves an anonymous constant by delegating to `resolve_anon_const_manual`, passing whether the expression is a trivial const argument and resolving the body expression through `resolve_expr`.

Sets up the scope rules for an anonymous constant based on its kind and generic-usage permissions, then resolves its body inside a constant rib and an elided-lifetime rib by calling `with_constant_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, and finally the supplied `resolve_expr` closure.

Main expression resolver that first calls `record_candidate_traits_for_expr_if_necessary`, then dispatches by expression kind to resolve paths with `smart_resolve_path`, labels with `resolve_label` and `report_error`, patterns with `resolve_pattern_top`, labeled constructs with `resolve_labeled_block` or `with_resolved_label`, nested blocks with `visit_block`, subexpressions with `resolve_expr`/`visit_expr`, path segments with `visit_path_segment`, and const arguments with `resolve_anon_const_manual`.

Precomputes trait candidates for field and method-call expressions by calling `traits_in_scope` on the accessed name and storing the resulting candidates for later diagnostics and method lookup assistance.
Queries the resolver for traits visible from the current scope and hygiene context that define the given name in the given namespace.

Resolves a rustdoc link path in a namespace using a per-module cache, delegating cache misses to `resolve_rustdoc_path` and suppressing non-local results that cannot safely be encoded for proc-macro metadata.

Processes doc attributes when configured to do so, resolves each referenced path across namespaces by calling `resolve_and_cache_rustdoc_path`, resolves prefixes for associated-item or diagnostic support, and when needed records trait candidates for doc-link lookup via `traits_in_scope`.

Visits an item, and for items with generics records how many generic lifetime parameters they declare. It calls `self.r.local_def_id` to obtain the item’s local definition id, inserts the computed count into `self.r.item_generics_num_lifetimes`, and then calls `visit::walk_item` to continue walking the item.

Drives the crate-level late name-resolution pass: it first calls `visit::walk_crate` with `ItemInfoCollector` to gather item information, then calls `LateResolutionVisitor::new` to create the main resolver visitor, calls `resolve_doc_links` to resolve crate attribute doc links, calls `visit::walk_crate` again to traverse the expanded crate for late resolution, and finally iterates over collected unused labels and calls `buffer_lint` to emit `UNUSED_LABELS` lints.

If an async body node is present, collects the lifetime parameters visible from the enclosing function context and records them for that async node in `extra_lifetime_params_map`. It calls `get`, `cloned`, and `unwrap_or_default` to start from any previously stored extra lifetime parameters for `fn_id`; iterates the lifetime ribs from innermost to outermost via `iter` and `rev`; calls `extend` and `map` to add each rib’s lifetime bindings; calls `get` again to merge previously created anonymous lifetime parameters from `AnonymousCreateParameter` binders; and finally calls `insert` to store the accumulated lifetime parameters for `async_node_id`. It stops at the first `Item` rib and treats any unexpected rib kind in this region as a bug.
